https://english.radio.cz/president-pavel.text: CS DE EN ES FR РУ УК President Pavel denies campaigning for re-election Facebook Twitter Czech President Petr Pavel says he has not yet decided whether to seek a second term and rejects claims that he is already campaigning for re-election. Speaking to CNN Prima News, Pavel said he plans to announce his decision in the middle of next year and would only begin campaigning after formally declaring his candidacy. Prime Minister Andrej Babiš (ANO) has repeatedly accused the president of already running a campaign. Pavel said his decision would depend primarily on his and his family’s health, as well as the level of public support for another presidential bid. Lithuania was in a minority of not supporting the resolution. The resolution, introduced by Togo and backed by members of the African Union, was approved by 164 countries. The United States was the only country to vote against it, while six countries â Estonia, Georgia, Moldova, Serbia, Ukraine and Lithuania â abstained. The resolution, titled Correct the Map, promotes the use of the Equal Earth projection, which more accurately represents the relative land areas of continents. UN vote on the Correct the Map resolution | UN The United States criticised the resolution, saying such initiatives contribute to the United Nations losing credibility. âInstead of focusing on genuine problems of international peace, prosperity, or good relations, this body is debating map projects from the 16th century, and their role in promoting reparations and cognitive justice,â US representative Yaryna Ferencevych said. However, the abstaining votes â coming exclusively from Central-Eastern Europe â quoted other reasons. Lithuaniaâs Foreign Ministry said its decision to abstain was prompted by the depiction of Crimea on the Equal Earth website, which was referenced in the resolution. âEqual Earthâ projekcija | AFP / Scanpix nuotr. âThe decision was prompted by references in the resolution to the Equal Earth website, where occupied Crimea is separated from Ukraine,â the ministry told LRT.lt. âAlthough the resolution seeks to more accurately depict the physical size of countries and continents, we cannot ignore inaccuracies in the depiction of the political map.â The ministry stressed that Lithuania does not recognise any redrawing of Ukraineâs territory by force. âWe support Ukraineâs sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders, including Crimea and all temporarily occupied territories,â it said. Ukraine also abstained from the vote and sharply criticised the depiction of Crimea. âIn 2026, the UN should not need a reminder: Crimea is Ukraine.. Shame,â Ukrainian lawmaker Kira Rudik said on X. Ukraine could not support the UN resolution on a new world map because it depicts occupied Crimea in a way that separates it from Ukraine. In 2026, the UN should not need a reminder: Crimea is Ukraine. Shame. pic.twitter.com/wcFMKGVnse — Kira Rudik (@kiraincongress) September 5, 2026 On the Equal Earth map, Ukraine is shown in a shade of green while Crimea is shown in grey. It is not, however, depicted as part of Russia. The United Nations has said the resolution does not prohibit the use of the Mercator projection, which was developed in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator for maritime navigation. Instead, the UN encourages governments, schools, international organisations and technology companies to use Equal Earth and other equal-area projections when the relative size of land areas is important. It also encourages education about the limitations of any flat map in representing the Earth, which is spherical. The Mercator projection was designed to preserve the shapes and angles of land masses for navigation, but it distorts their relative size. The distortion becomes more pronounced toward the poles as a three-dimensional globe is represented on a two-dimensional surface. As a result, Europe and North America appear much larger, while Africa and South America appear smaller than their actual relative areas. A group of cartographers introduced the Equal Earth projection in 2018. Unlike the Mercator projection, it preserves the relative areas of continents while seeking to maintain their shapes as they appear on a globe. Africa, Latin America, South Asia and Oceania consequently appear substantially larger on an Equal Earth map. LRT English Newsletter Every Friday morning. Thanks for subscribing!
